newsitem.title: SPAIN: ATHLETICS-WORLD HALF MARATHON TITLES FOR CHINA AND ITALY.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-WORLD HALF MARATHON TITLES FOR CHINA AND ITALY.

text.p: Italian Stefano Baldini and China's Xiujuan Ren both won their first major international titles with victories in the men's and women's events in the world half marathon championships on Sunday.
Baldini won the men's title in one hour one minute 17 seconds to lead Italy to the team gold. Josephat Kiprono of Kenya was second in 1:01:30 and Zimbabwe's Tendai Chimusasa third in 1:02:00.
Baldini, 25, battled with pre-race favourite Kiprono over the final five kilometres but edged ahead with the finish in sight to win by 30 metres.
Chimusasa capturing the bronze after a sprint for the line with Spaniard Carlos De La Torre.
"I can't believe it. This is my first major international medal," said Baldini. "I never expected to win with all the Africans in the field."
Spain finished second in the men's team contest, just ahead of Japan who were third. The Kenyans, winners of the men's team title on all four previous occasions, had to settle for fourth.
Xiujuan, a 20-year-old economics student, was not completely satisfied with her time of 1:10:39, saying she had hoped to set a world best mark for the 21.097-km race.
She said she has run faster in training than the world best of 1:07:11 set by Briton Liz McColgan in Tokyo on January, 1992.

McColgan, who had hoped to make amends for her poor marathon performance at the Atlanta Olympics where she finished 16th, dropped out after 16 kms while lying seventh, suffering from a tight hamstring.

Romanians filled the next three places behind Xiujian to take the women's team title for the fourth successive time. Lidia Simon was second in 1:10:57, Aura Buia third with 1:11:01 and Nutu Olaru fourth in 1:11:07.

Xiujuan said: "I had a cold three days ago and I suffered in the hot conditions. I also won the national 5,000 metres and 10,000 metres last week and I'm exhausted and was not in a good mood to face another championship."
